spatial_claims.claim: Points A, D, E, C lie in that order along line AC (collinear, ordered)
Lines AB and AC form an angle at A; triangle ABC is formed by joining B to C
DF is drawn parallel to BC, with D on AC and F on AB; F is between A and G on AB
EG is drawn parallel to BC, with E on AC and G on AB; G is between F and B on AB
DF is parallel to EG (both parallel to BC, by transitivity)
In triangle ABC, D is on side AC, F is on side AB, DF parallel to BC — configuration for 6.2
In triangle ABC, E is on side AC, G is on side AB, EG parallel to BC — configuration for 6.2
Triangle AEG exists as sub-triangle; D on side AE (between A and E), F on side AG (between A and G), DF parallel to EG — configuration for 6.2

configuration_map: Line AC: A --- D --- E --- C (ordered collinear). Line AB: A --- F --- G --- B (ordered collinear, order established by parallels from nearer points on AC hitting AB nearer to A). Triangle ABC formed by joining B to C. Three parallel lines DF, EG, BC cut through triangle ABC. Sub-triangle AEG: vertices A (common), E (on AC), G (on AB). Within sub-triangle AEG, point D lies on side AE and point F lies on side AG, with DF parallel to the opposite side EG. All point positions are consistent across every step of the proof.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The point orderings on both lines (A-D-E-C and A-F-G-B) are correctly established and maintained. Each application of Proposition 6.2 uses a valid configuration: a line parallel to one side of a triangle cutting the other two sides at interior points. The sub-triangle AEG in Step 7 is legitimate (A, E, G are non-collinear) with D and F properly on its sides. No angle decompositions, no inside/outside claims, and no circle arguments are involved. The proof relies on parallel lines and proportion theory with straightforward, consistent spatial configurations throughout.
